title: Name the medium in every prompt
rule: Put the medium word (claymation, paper cutout, flat 2D, 3D cartoon) in every clip prompt and every picture prompt, never only in the first.
why: Models carry no memory between generations and revert to photorealism when the style block is missing.
how: Prefix: "Claymation, polymer clay, matte, thumbprints. " then the shot. Same words in every clip.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js makeFace/makePlate prompts carry only Illustration or Photograph from mediumOf; the look description is not repeated
monofilm.idea: Prefix each clip prompt with the look desc (medium, material, lighting) from the chosen look.

title: Say clay, felt or paper, not just stop motion
rule: Name the exact material, not the generic technique.
why: Stop motion also covers puppets and cut-outs; the material name picks the texture.
how: "Plasticine clay figure" versus "felt puppet" versus "paper cutout, flat layered card, snipped edges".

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js isDrawn / isHandmade (felt, paper, puppet, clay, stop-motion, vector, watercolour and more)

title: Ask for handmade imperfections and ban the polished words
rule: Add fingerprints, seams, matte finish and slight wobble, and avoid smooth, glossy, perfect, polished.
why: Polish words pull output toward a clean 3D render; imperfections signal handmade.
how: "visible thumbprints, seams where pieces join, matte not shiny, slight clay imperfections".

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js READ_SYSTEM: handmade looks must name the material and its traces
monofilm.idea: Add the handmade-texture phrase to clip prompts too

title: Pair positive medium words with a short ban list
rule: Add a short exclusion list (photorealism, smooth CGI, live action) next to the positive medium description, and let the positive words do most of the work.
why: Positive-only prompts let realism leak back; negatives alone rarely force a cartoon look. Veo wants excluded things listed without the word no.
how: Positive: "claymation, matte clay". Exclude: "photorealism, smooth 3D rendering, live action".

monofilm.where: src/picturecheck.js checks medium after the fact; no ban list is added to prompts
monofilm.idea: Append an exclusion line for the opposite medium to every drawn-look prompt.

title: Light a handmade look like a small set
rule: Use one practical lamp or soft window light and hard small shadows, not cinematic soft gradients.
why: Soft diffuse light breaks the miniature tabletop read.
how: "single warm desk lamp from upper right, hard shadow edges, visible set edges".

monofilm.idea: Put tabletop lighting words into stop-motion look descriptions.

title: Ask for stepped motion in words; do not trust an fps setting
rule: For a stop-motion feel write "12fps, slightly stepped, held poses, no motion blur" in the prompt and expect only an approximation.
why: Models default to smooth interpolation; sources treat 12fps as prompt language, not a real setting.
how: "stepped 12fps motion with brief holds on each pose, crisp frames, no motion blur".

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip: Motion feel line for handmade looks

title: Fix frame-rate feel in post when the model refuses
rule: If a clip comes out too smooth, drop it to 12 fps with each frame held twice in the edit.
why: On twos is the real stop-motion and Spider-Verse technique; a post pass gives it for certain.
how: Conform to 24 fps and hold each pair of frames; mix ones and twos so the hero moves smoothly.

monofilm.idea: Optional ffmpeg step: fps=12 then fps=24 on clips of a stop-motion look.

title: Pick one animation style word and never swap synonyms
rule: Keep one identical style phrase across all prompts; do not alternate cartoon, illustrated and animated.
why: Swapping terms causes drift; two equal styles give muddy results and anime plus 3D plus cinematic compete.
how: Choose "soft 3D cartoon" once and paste it; make a second style only an accent.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js look.look/name is stored once; READ_SYSTEM makes desc name the medium
monofilm.idea: Compose the same look string verbatim into every clip prompt.

title: Lock the style with reference pictures, then keep prompts short
rule: Approve a style reference picture or a batch of them and reuse it in every generation; keep text for motion only.
why: A picture carries the look better than words and prevents conflicting descriptions.
how: 20 to 30 style frames for a short; style reference slot in the tool; text says what moves.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip with film.pictures; look chosen then faces and plates drawn in it

title: Approve a still in the style before animating
rule: Get the first frame of each clip approved as an image in the locked style before spending video credits.
why: Stills are cheaper to review than video and drift is caught early.
how: Review start frame, then generate motion from it plus character references.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js makeFrame start/end frames with drawChecked

title: Give each character a few strong identity traits and a silhouette
rule: Design recurring cartoon characters with a distinct silhouette, one main colour and one unmistakable feature, and no changing clothes.
why: Fewer distinct traits are easier to repeat; wide shots rely on silhouette and colour, and photoreal styles expose small face differences.
how: "a round yellow duckling, huge eyes, one red bow". Test: fill black, is it still recognisable.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js READ_SYSTEM people desc: identity in the body, no clothes, one big shape; picturecheck compares appearance

title: Prefer colour-coded identity over clothing
rule: Make each character recognisable by body colour and shape, and avoid outfits that change.
why: Garments drift most between shots; two or three colours per character with a reserved accent hold.
how: Give each character one body colour not used by another, and keep it in every prompt.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js READ_SYSTEM asks for main colour in the body and at most one garment; no check that colours differ between characters
monofilm.idea: Warn when two characters share a main colour.

title: Write anticipation and follow-through into the clip beat
rule: State a lead-in beat before the action and secondary movement after it.
why: Models jump straight into the main action and freeze hair and loose cloth; a described lead-in gives readable timing.
how: "she glances down and takes a breath, then jumps; her scarf keeps swinging when she lands".

monofilm.idea: Add an optional anticipation and settle line to the clip writer for drawn looks.

title: Use squash and stretch and exaggeration only in drawn looks
rule: Ask for squash on impact and stretch in fast motion for cartoons, and keep it subtle or absent in photographic looks.
why: Exaggeration is permitted by a stylised look; volume should stay constant.
how: "soft squash on landing, quick stretch on the jump, volume preserved".

monofilm.idea: Gate a squash-and-stretch phrase on isDrawn(look).

title: Describe motion on arcs and one action per clip
rule: Describe turns and swings as curves and give each clip a single action.
why: Quick turns give unnaturally straight paths, and several actions in one prompt give messy motion.
how: "he swings his arm in a wide arc" and nothing else; 5 to 8 seconds.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js clipBeats splits a scene into clip beats
monofilm.idea: Check each beat holds a single action.

title: Never leave the medium unchecked: a photo in a cartoon is the commonest failure
rule: Check every picture for medium and reject a photograph in an illustrated film or the reverse.
why: Style delusion is documented and the prompt, source image or preset can carry realism cues.
how: Compare each picture with the medium word; also audit reference images and presets.

monofilm.where: src/picturecheck.js kind medium plus mediumOf in public/js/wizard-model.js; faces and plates pass medium to drawChecked

title: Do not mix live action and animation in one clip unless it is a separate layer
rule: Keep photographic and drawn elements in separate shots or composited layers with their own lighting.
why: A single generation tends to turn the realistic characters cartoonish or the reverse; real footage should stay for exact faces or products.
how: Generate the drawn layer on its own and match lighting; keep real footage for faces that must stay exact.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js mediumOf is binary (illustration or photograph)
monofilm.idea: Declare mixed films as per-shot medium and refuse a mixed medium inside one clip.

title: Generate three to five takes per handmade clip
rule: Plan to roll several takes and keep the best texture.
why: Texture quality varies a lot between rolls; one source reports about three generations per usable shot.
how: Budget three takes for stop-motion looks; pick by texture and pacing.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js retry on failed checks; no multi-take pick
monofilm.idea: Offer a take picker on clips of handmade looks.

title: Slow, plain pacing and no flashing for young children
rule: For ages 3 to 5 use slow pacing, one idea at a time, gentle transitions, no flashing or loud sudden audio, and a clear beginning, middle and end.
why: Expert guidance and a news report on young viewers say fast, plotless content is a concern.
how: Hold shots longer, one new thing every 30 to 60 seconds, soft fades; sound-off test.

monofilm.idea: Add an audience setting that slows cuts and bans flash transitions.

title: Review every kids film in full, for strange faces and unnatural poses
rule: Watch every clip yourself before release and reject eerie faces or unnatural animal poses.
why: AI videos for children have been criticised as unsafe and low value; platforms may not label animated AI content.
how: Run a checklist: whole video watched, no flashing, gentle audio, age-appropriate words, positive tone.

monofilm.idea: Add a kids-safety pass on the final cut.

title: Use bold flat colour blocks with a capped palette for minimalist looks
rule: Cap the palette at a few named colours, ask for solid blocks, no gradients, no shadows, crisp edges.
why: Flat looks need explicit bans on shading, or the model adds it.
how: "flat 2D, solid colour blocks, 3 colours (teal, cream, coral), no gradients, no shadows, bold outlines".

monofilm.idea: Allow a palette field in the look and add it to all prompts.

title: Regenerate from the reference when a drawn character drifts
rule: When a shot goes off model, fix the reference and regenerate that shot, not re-describe in text.
why: Retyped descriptions reintroduce drift; fixing at the source holds for later scenes.
how: Return to the closest reference angle and redo only the affected shot.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js makeFace variants A B C; picturecheck appearance retry
monofilm.idea: Make a drift fix re-anchor on the reference face.
